result.title: Capability-Driven Self-Evolution of Agent Memory
result.summary: Memory self-evolution uses task feedback to iteratively improve executable memory programs that store and retrieve information from past interactions. Existing approaches typically adopt holistic evolution, deriving revision directions from mixed feedback and judging progress by overall performance. This can obscure optimization directions and hide capability-specific gains offset by regressions elsewhere, leaving promising directions underexplored. We introduce capability-driven evolution, which extends search guidance from overall performance to individual capability dimensions, preserving promising revisions and expanding exploration beyond the boundaries of holistic evolution. We propose PrisMem, which uses dependency-aware capability selection to prioritize targets with potential cross-capability benefits and history-guided diagnosis to refine capability specialists. Trace-guided integration compares evaluated programs on paired differential cases, using their behavioral differences to consolidate complementary gains into a unified memory program. Experiments show that PrisMem outperforms the strongest baselines by 10.54 and 7.83 percentage points on BEAM-1M and LongMemEval-M, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness on million-token histories.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出能力驱动的记忆自演化方法 PrisMem，用依赖感知的能力选择、历史引导诊断和轨迹引导的差分案例整合，分维度演化可执行的记忆程序，在百万 token 长历史基准上超过整体式演化基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按能力维度拆分优化目标、并以差分案例定位行为差异的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中贡献分配、监督信号设计与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 各自收益归因的问题。
